To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the EBV-LMP2,4 may be the specific T cell stimulating and target antigens in NPC and EBV-IgAVCA+ patients.

(i) EBV-LMP2 and EBNA4 may be major specific T cell antigens and target antigens of CTL responses; and (ii) EBV-LM1 may be not only major specific T cell antigen but also the target antigen of CTL response in NPC patients.
EBV-LCLs are able to stimulate CTL responses against EBV antigens LMP2 and EBNA4 in normal individuals and NPC patients.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the recognition of EBV specific T cell responses and the responses against EBV target antigens in NPC patients and normal individuals.
the EBV-specific CTL immune responses of NPC patients, EBV-IgAVCA+ patients and normal individuals.
the recognition and responses of CTL against target antigens in NPC patients and normal individuals.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
LMP1 and 2 are the major EBV specific CTL stimulating antigens in NPC patients and normal individuals.
EBV specific CTL response is present in normal individuals and NPC patients and the target antigen may be EBV-LMP2 and EBNA1,4.
the CTL responses against EBV antigens are not significantly impaired in patients with NPC.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the EBV specific CTL immune responses against EBV LMP2 and EBNA4 are not only found in NPC patients and EBV-IgG/VCA+ patients but also in normal individuals.
LMP1 and LMP2 may be the major target antigens for EBV specific CTL immune responses, but LMP1 is not the major target antigents for EBV specific T cell stimulation.
EBV specific CTL response is a complex and multi-target immune responses.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the EBV specific CTL immune responses are not impaired in untreated NPC patients, which may be a good prognostic factor for these patients.
LMP1, 2 and EBNA1,4 may play an important role in the development of EBV specific T cell response and NPC pathogenesis.
EBV specific CTL immune responses against target antigens may be a potential approach for the prevention of NPC.
